headline: Apple reportedly launching 'Upgrade' program for iPhones, Macs, and iPads
summary: The new lease-to-own service, backed by Klarna, is expected to launch on July 28th, offering 24-36 month leases for various Apple devices.
details: Apple is reportedly preparing to launch a new 'Apple Upgrade' program, a lease-to-own service for its devices. Backed by Klarna, the program is expected to debut on July 28th, replacing the current iPhone Upgrade Program and standard financing options.

The service will offer 24-month leases for iPhones and Apple Watches, and 36-month leases for iPads and Macs. It aims to make high-end devices more accessible amid rising component costs and price increases.

However, not all devices will be eligible; budget models like the base iPad, iPhone 16, Apple Watch SE, and MacBook Neo are reportedly excluded. Unlike the previous program, AppleCare will not be included, which is also seeing price hikes.

This move follows Apple's recent price increases across many products, though iPhones were not part of that round. The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro series is also anticipated to bring higher pricing later this year.
caption:
Apple is reportedly launching a new 'Upgrade' program, allowing users to lease iPhones, Macs, and iPads. It's like a car lease for your tech, with options to upgrade or keep devices.

Apple is reportedly preparing to launch a new 'Apple Upgrade' program, a lease-to-own service for its devices. Backed by Klarna, the program is expected to debut on July 28th, replacing the current iPhone Upgrade Program and standard financing options.

The service will offer 24-month leases for iPhones and Apple Watches, and 36-month leases for iPads and Macs. It aims to make high-end devices more accessible amid rising component costs and price increases.

However, not all devices will be eligible; budget models like the base iPad, iPhone 16, Apple Watch SE, and MacBook Neo are reportedly excluded. Unlike the previous program, AppleCare will not be included, which is also seeing price hikes.

This move follows Apple's recent price increases across many products, though iPhones were not part of that round. The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro series is also anticipated to bring higher pricing later this year.
